en: The Jātaka:
The Collection of Tens,
Chapter on the Four Gates (Catudvāravagga)
8. The Takkalājātaka “There are no *takkalas*, no *āluvās*,
no *biḷālis*, nor *kaḷambas*, my dear.”
“O father, for what purpose do you dig a pit in the midst of a charnel ground in the forest?
“O father, your grandfather is very weak;”
Afflicted by many diseases and suffering,
I shall bury him in a pit;
for I no longer find any pleasure in his life.
“Having conceived this evil intention,
you are performing a cruel deed that will bring you great harm.
Dear one, you yourself shall surely receive [the consequences] from me.”
"Driven by such karma,
following that same course of conduct as a slave,
I too shall bury you in a pit."
“Addressing me with harsh words,
you assail me, O prince;
though you are my own legitimate son.”
"You are one who wishes me ill, my son.
"I do not wish you ill, father;
I too, father, am one who wishes you well."
"I am not able to restrain one who is performing such evil karma.
"Whoever has abandoned his mother or father..."
For the one of evil nature harms those who do no harm;
with the breakup of the body, after death,
he undoubtedly goes to hell.
Whoever has served his mother or father with food and drink,
at the breaking up of the body, in the life hereafter—
Without doubt, he goes to a happy destination.
My son, you are not one who feels compassion for my harm;
you, my son, are one who feels compassion for my welfare.
"And though I was being spoken to thus by my mother,
I committed such a cruel deed.
"That wife of yours who was of ignoble character— "
This mother of mine is your own Sakyan kinswoman;
she would drive you out from your own home,
and she might even bring you further suffering.
She who was your wife of ignoble form is now my mother, my own Sakyan birth-giver;
she is tamed like a female elephant brought under control.
“May that woman of evil character be born again!
Thus ends the eighth Jātaka, the Takkala-jātaka.
